title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is grappling with cost concerns and launch risks, particularly highlighted by the GAO's recent report on the Space Force portfolio. Meanwhile, funding continues to flow into various sectors, with notable investments in satellite technology and emerging startups.

themes.title: Cost Concerns for Space Force
themes.body: The GAO has flagged rising satellite costs and launch risks in the Space Force's portfolio, raising eyebrows about budget management. As the military pushes for resilience, the financial implications could ripple across contractors.

themes.title: Funding Boosts for Startups
themes.body: Recent funding rounds, including True Anomaly's $190M Series C and Hongqing's $191M raise, signal a robust interest in space technology. Investors seem undeterred by the challenges of the sector, betting on its long-term potential.

themes.title: Launch Activity Picks Up
themes.body: Isar Aerospace's recent contract for a Planet imaging satellite and Pegasus's Swift reboost mission highlight a busy launch calendar. This uptick suggests that despite risks, demand for satellite deployment remains strong.

themes.title: Defense Tech IPOs on the Horizon
themes.body: The defense-tech sector is eyeing a potential IPO window, with companies like Palantir and others extending contracts to bolster their positions. As the market shifts, expect more startups to position themselves for public offerings.
